summary: Recorded the repeated-rounds receipt, which changes the impact from a one-off index shift to a drift. Updates: the parent interpretation is a complete six-receipt account (violated/asserted) stating the drift, the two-inflated-reporter requirement for the leader-side decision, the same-run controls, and limitations saying the drift was exercised for three rounds with no bound established, that compaction was not exercised and that the consequence stays within index accounting and readability because the sealed configuration accepts no further entries; the inflation behaviour now records that each further re-synchronization adds one index; a new behaviour records the cluster-level drift of the reported accepted and decided indices; and the question's discriminator now asks whether anything bounds the drift (counter or storage limit, later leader change) and whether it carries into the instances started for the next configuration.
